items.title: Trump waives Russia oil sanctions; HDFC, Axis, ICICI Bank in focus | Opening Bell
items.summary: Dalal Street starts the week after a second straight weekly gain, led by IT stocks, which jumped 10% for their best week since 2008. GIFT Nifty points to a quiet start. FIIs sold equities for a ninth straight week (Rs 8,991 crore), though they bought Rs 1,166 crore on Friday, while DIIs bought Rs 7,813 crore. The rupee gained 2% last week, its best weekly gain in seven months. Global cues are cautious: the Nasdaq lost over 4% last week on a chip-stock slide, Asian markets are down over 1% in Japan and Korea, and US 10-year yields sit above 5.08%. Brent pulled back from $110 amid Ukraine-Russia and Strait of Hormuz tensions, while Trump waived the Russia sanctions that threatened 100% tariffs on India. Eyes are on Q2 results from Bajaj Finance, Infosys, Eternal, UltraTech, Dr Reddy’s and BPCL, plus the Rs 30,213 crore Jio Platforms and Rs 1,450 crore Paras Health IPOs opening October 21. Join us live for key levels and stock ideas.

CareEdge Global IFSC to sell 19.8% stake to State Bank of India, NSEIX
CareEdge Global IFSC to sell 19.8% stake to State Bank of India, NSEIX
items.summary:
Care Edge Ratings on Monday said it has decided to sell a 19.8 per cent stake in its wholly-owned subsidiary CareEdge Global IFSC to State Bank of India and NSE IFSC.
The company has executed share purchase agreements and a shareholders' agreement with State Bank of India (SBI) and NSE IFSC (NSEIX) to sell a 9.9 per cent equity stake each in CareEdge Global IFSC Ltd (CGIL), Care Edge Ratings said in a regulatory filing.
After the share transfer is completed, the company will continue to hold an 80.2 per cent equity stake in CGIL, it said.
The deal is expected to be concluded within two months, it added.

CareEdge Global IFSC to sell 19.8% stake to State Bank of India, NSEIX
items.summary:
Care Edge Ratings on Monday said it has decided to sell a 19.8 per cent stake in its wholly-owned subsidiary CareEdge Global IFSC to State Bank of India and NSE IFSC.
The company has executed share purchase agreements and a shareholders' agreement with State Bank of India (SBI) and NSE IFSC (NSEIX) to sell a 9.9 per cent equity stake each in CareEdge Global IFSC Ltd (CGIL), Care Edge Ratings said in a regulatory filing.
After the share transfer is completed, the company will continue to hold an 80.2 per cent equity stake in CGIL, it said.
The deal is expected to be concluded within two months, it added.

CareEdge Global IFSC to sell 19.8% stake to State Bank of India, NSEIX
items.summary:
Care Edge Ratings on Monday said it has decided to sell a 19.8 per cent stake in its wholly-owned subsidiary CareEdge Global IFSC to State Bank of India and NSE IFSC.
The company has executed share purchase agreements and a shareholders' agreement with State Bank of India (SBI) and NSE IFSC (NSEIX) to sell a 9.9 per cent equity stake each in CareEdge Global IFSC Ltd (CGIL), Care Edge Ratings said in a regulatory filing.
After the share transfer is completed, the company will continue to hold an 80.2 per cent equity stake in CGIL, it said.
The deal is expected to be concluded within two months, it added.
